threads_text: The Justice Department is asking how NVIDIA's $12.9 billion purchase of Hugging Face would affect competition in AI, Reuters reports. Hugging Face is where developers share millions of open models, and NVIDIA promised it would stay open. Should a chip giant own the place where open AI lives?

paragraphs.text: The US Department of Justice has asked how Nvidia's $12.93 billion deal to buy the open source AI platform Hugging Face would affect competition in artificial intelligence, Reuters reported on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, citing two people familiar with the matter.

According to Reuters, officials asked whether the acquisition would allow Nvidia to capture "a fundamental distribution point for AI." The Next Web, summarizing the report, said officials also wanted to know whether Nvidia could use Hugging Face to disadvantage rivals.

Nvidia announced the agreement on September 3, 2026. Hugging Face, founded in 2016, is a platform where developers publish and download open AI models, datasets and applications. It hosts more than 3 million models, 1 million applications and 500,000 datasets, and has more than 18 million users, according to iClarified's report on the deal announcement.

In his blog post announcing the deal, Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang wrote that Hugging Face "will remain an open platform for the entire AI ecosystem," Semafor reported. Nvidia said developers would not need Nvidia hardware to build on or deploy through the platform, and that it would keep supporting open weight models and multiple clouds and chip makers. Semafor described the purchase as Nvidia's second largest deal. Nvidia has said it expects the acquisition to close in the first half of 2027.

Reuters reported that the questions come as antitrust enforcers pursue a years long investigation into Nvidia's conduct that began under President Joe Biden and has continued under President Donald Trump. That probe covers Nvidia's acquisitions, investments and sales practices, including whether the company has pressured customers. According to Reuters, the department has also examined Nvidia's December 2025 acquisition of SchedMD, its 2025 licensing and hiring deal with chip startup Groq, and its earlier purchase of Run:ai.

A Justice Department spokesperson declined to comment on specific matters, Reuters reported. Nvidia declined to comment, and Hugging Face did not respond to requests for comment. Reuters noted that government investigations are not evidence of wrongdoing and do not necessarily lead to lawsuits.

In NeuraFeed's reading, the inquiry goes to the heart of why the deal drew attention in September. Nvidia is best known as a chip company, and Hugging Face is one of the main places where developers share and discover open models. Bringing the two under one owner is the kind of combination antitrust officials tend to examine closely, even when the buyer promises to keep the platform open to everyone.

The next step to watch is whether the Justice Department opens a formal merger review of the deal before its planned closing in the first half of 2027, or asks Nvidia for commitments on keeping Hugging Face open.
